newsitem.title: USA: Cash crude markets remain firm in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Cash crude markets remain firm in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices extended their run higher Tuesday afternoon on the back of firming futures prices, while grades also remained strong in a fundamentally bullish prompt market.
August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was charted around 45 cents firmer at $20.20-30 a barrel, pulling even and then posting stronger numbers than second month September WTI.

Current August/September spreads, or rolls, were put at 1-3 cents in favor of August. WTI/Cushing Postings Plus business accelerated gains to move to the $2.01-03 level off the switch in spread premiums, traders said.

Fundamentals in the North Sea market bolstered domestic differentials in the U.S. Gulf. A pair of Brent cargoes loading July 12-14 were done at an average value of August Brent -10 cents, reflecting tight supply amid active demand.

Current talk in the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James market put the grade at 20-23 cents over August WTI/Cushing. August LLS has gained steadily since taking over from July as the active month, reflecting a lack of Brent fixtures to the U.S. Gulf and tight arbitrage levels.

West Texas Sour/Midland barrels also saw interest perk-up from refiners in the morning with deals done at $1.08 and $1.10 under the marker. Current market chatter put WTS at a $1.00-05 discount to August WTI/Cushing.
Other grade talk had Eugene Island barrels pegged at $1.25 under WTI/Cushing, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 20 cents below benchmark.
